item.title: Self-dual indecomposable KLR projectives give the lower global basis (symmetric type)
item.statement: Assume the Cartan datum of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] has symmetric Cartan matrix $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and uses the quiver normalization $d_i=1$ for every i, the field $k$ has characteristic $0$, and the KLR parameters are the quiver-geometric ones (the specialization attached to a finite quiver without loops, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities $h_{ij}$ and $a_{ij}=-(h_{ij}+h_{ji})$: $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ for $i\ne j$, in the fixed native crossing-sign convention; arbitrary parameter changes, including a global replacement by $u+v$, require their own proved gauge equivalence). Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the contravariant graded projective duality $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$ ($P\cong P^\#$ after the unique normalizing shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. No extension to arbitrary KLR parameters or to non-symmetric Cartan data is asserted here; any such extension requires its own parameter-change invariance theorem.
item.strategy:
The only remaining held prerequisite is the SEMISIMPLE QUIVER-FLAG EXT REALIZATION, in the full symmetric d_i=1/characteristic0/loopless-quiver parameter scope including arbitrary edge multiplicities. Construct delta L=sum_nu (pi_nu)!k[dim Ftilde_nu] on E_V; prove its decomposition into shifts of simple equivariant perverse sheaves and the graded isomorphism R(beta)=Ext_G^*(delta L,delta L) with the actual native signs and VV multiplication convention (a*b is categorical b composed with a, so R is the opposite of the ordinary categorical End algebra). VV1.3 assumes semisimple proper pushforward, and its Theorem3.6 uses the Ext/Borel-Moore convolution comparison, localization and affine-paving computation. Those geometric foundations still have no proved local suppliers. BBD6.2.5/6.2.7 imports arithmetic purity; its mere citation is not a local proof. Full ext/flag realization remains held, not weakened to finite ADE or simple edges.
Once that realization is proved, no separate equivariant-formality/base-change theorem is needed for this route. The graded Yoneda functor Y_T=Ext_G^*(delta L,T) gives a fully faithful equivalence from add(delta L shifts) to finite graded projective R-modules: verify it on the generator delta L by Hom_R(R,R)=R^op=End_DG(delta L) with ordinary categorical composition, extend to finite sums/shifts, and restrict to idempotent summands. Each simple perverse summand T belongs to that additive category after a shift. Therefore End_R^*(Y_T)=Ext_G^*(T,T). For perverse T the heart orthogonality gives Hom_DG(T,T[m])=0 for m<0, so this algebra has no negative degrees; its degree-zero part is the division algebra End(T). Thus Y_T is indecomposable. The same additive equivalence exhausts all indecomposable projective shift orbits. The algebraic maximal-tail supplier already proves every simple R-module absolutely simple; a division degree-zero endomorphism algebra of a projective cover injects into its simple-head scalar ring, so End_R^0(Y_T)=k. This proves the essential positive-End property without VV4.8 augmentation/formality and without relying on a generalized geometric canonical comparison.
By the separately proved generic projective-duality supplier every projective orbit has a unique #-self-dual representative P_b. Put x_b=gamma^-1[P_b]. It is integral and bar fixed. The exact Hom/tensor comparison for a self-dual P gives B_L(x_b,x_b)=h(P_b,P_b)=1+q N[[q]], since the geometric End property is unchanged by grading shifts. Dividing by C_beta=1 moduloq gives B_K(x_b,x_b) in1+q Z[[q]]. The general QG5 half norm criterion therefore places x_b in the q0 crystal lattice. Bar fixes it, so it also lies in the actual bar chart; integral balanced globalization writes x_b as a finite Z-linear combination of lower global vectors. Their residue Gram matrix is the identity; norm residue1 forces the sum of coefficient squares to be1. Thus x_b is exactly plus or minus one lower global vector. Distinct projective shift orbits are independent and have the same finite weight cardinality as the global basis by the integral K_0 isomorphism, so they exhaust this signed set.
The new positive divided-string leading-term supplier removes every minus sign using its integral LEFT-string ideal equality, coefficient1 projective adjunction and the general adapted LEFT global recursion from1. It retains the full symmetric claim and does not use batch8's finite-ADE canonical-comparison item. The based quotient then follows from the general QG5 zero/survival projection. All algebraic steps and this conditional deduction are local; the exact semisimple quiver-flag Ext realization remains the genuine held geometric result.

Assume AC as declared, inherited from the equivariant, flag-bundle and Euler/Chern suppliers. Sources: Varagnolo-Vasserot, Canonical bases and KLR-algebras, SS1.7-1.9 (the convolution algebra acting on the canonical module and the grading shifts; PDF pp. 7-8), SS2.5-2.9 (relative-position orbits, closures and the convolution inclusions used for the filtration; PDF pp. 9-11), SS2.13-2.21 (torus localization, the Euler classes $\Lambda_w$ and the fixed-point formulas proving faithfulness; PDF pp. 12-15) and SS2.26-2.27 (the free $F_V$-module PBW statement, whose cell proof is left to the reader and is supplied here; PDF pp. 19); Ginzburg, Geometric methods in representation theory, SS1 (the Borel-Moore exact sequence, fundamental classes and the intersection pairing; PDF pp. 4-7) and SS2 (convolution with supports; PDF pp. 7-11); Rouquier, Quiver Hecke algebras and 2-Lie algebras, SS5.4.4 (the corner Ext groups are free graded $H^ ullet(BG)$-modules of computable rank; PDF pp. 43-44).
Step 1 (orbit and stratum decomposition). For fixed $
u$ and $w\in S_m$ the relative-position pair orbit $O_{w,
u}$ is a single $G$-orbit whose stabilizer has a maximal torus and a unipotent remainder; its projection to the first flag is an affine Schubert-cell fibration, and over $O_{w,
u}$ the incidence variety $Z_{w
u,
u}$ is the associated vector bundle with fiber $U_F\cap U_{F'}$. This is the internal Gaussian-elimination and row-echelon argument; the published finite-field relative-position theorem is not used. Its equivariant BM module is a shift of $H_G^ ullet(O)=H_{B\cap wB'w^{-1}}^ ullet(\mathrm{pt})=k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$, because the unipotent part of the stabilizer is contractible.
Step 2 (closure basis). Order relative positions by a linear extension of Bruhat order so that the successive unions of closures are closed. The closed/open Borel-Moore exact sequence from [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]] (support localization) has vanishing odd terms, hence degenerates into short exact sequences in each even degree; the fundamental class of the closure of each stratum restricts to the stratum class and generates the rank-one polynomial quotient. Multiplication by arbitrary first-flag polynomials gives explicit lifts, so the closure fundamental classes form a free left polynomial-module basis, one for each compatible pair $(w,
u)$.
Step 3 (faithfulness). Refine the orbit decomposition by torus-stable Schubert cells: each piece is an affine space with one fixed point and nonzero line-character weights (no arrow weight vanishes, because the quiver is loopless). The closed/open sequences and the vector-bundle Thom and Euler self-intersection calculus of [[lem-complex-oriented-diagonal-thom-class-realizes-the-six-functor-exchange-on-supports]] show that $H_T^{\mathrm{BM}}(Z)$ and $H_T^{\mathrm{BM}}(X)$ are free over the torus polynomial ring $S_T$, and that inverting the finitely many nonzero weights makes fixed-point pushforward an isomorphism, cell by cell; the fixed-pair supported classes multiply as matrix units, so the localized action on $ igoplus_
u H_T^{\mathrm{BM}}(X_
u)$ is faithful. Freeness descends faithfulness to the unlocalized $T$-action, and the restriction $H_G^{\mathrm{BM}}	o H_T^{\mathrm{BM}}$ is injective by the even Schubert-cell filtration of the flag bundle, whose Leray-Hirsch freeness over $H_G^ ullet(\mathrm{pt})$ is [[thm-leray-hirsch-module-isomorphism]] applied at each stage of the projective-bundle tower, with the finite-stage CW structure of [[thm-schubert-cells-give-the-stable-grassmannian-cw-structure]] and the tautological Euler-class fiber generator of [[lem-complex-tautological-euler-class-restricts-to-the-projective-fiber-generator]]. The fiber basis over the arbitrary characteristic-zero field is obtained from the integral basis by extension of coefficients; the published tautological-Euler lemma is stated for $\mathbb Z$ and $\mathbb F_p$, and its free cellular model is the part extended. Hence the $G$-action on $P= igoplus_
u H_G^ ullet(X_
u)[d_
u]$ is faithful.

u$ form a polynomial basis (the change-of-basis matrix from closure classes is triangular with diagonal $\pm1$). [AC as declared]
